# Recognition Pulse: a synthetic-data analytics project

Live site: sarangsoman.netlify.app (home, /teardown, /dashboard, /assistant). Code for the data and analysis is in `analysis/`; the AI draft function is `netlify/functions/draft.mjs`.

A small, reproducible project that shows how to read the health of an employee recognition program.
**All data is synthetic.** It is generated by `generate_data.py` (seed 2026), so anyone can reproduce every number.

## What is in here

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `generate_data.py` | Builds 600 employees, 67 teams, 24 weeks of recognitions, redemptions and a planted A/B test |
| `build_dashboard_data.py` | Computes the dashboard numbers and runs the A/B analysis (baseline-adjusted regression) |
| `dashboard.html` | The published dashboard (same page that is on the web) |
| `data/*.csv` | Load these into Power BI, Excel or SQL |

## Data dictionary

| File | One row is | Key columns |
|---|---|---|
| `employees.csv` | an employee | `employee_id`, `department`, `team_id`, `manager_id`, `level`, `join_date`, `invited_date`, `first_login_date`, `first_recognition_sent_date`, `first_redemption_date` |
| `teams.csv` | a team | `team_id`, `department`, `manager_id`, `headcount` |
| `recognitions.csv` | a recognition | `date`, `giver_id` (`SYSTEM` for automatic milestones), `receiver_id`, `type`, `points`, `company_value`, `channel`, `ai_assisted`, `message_words` |
| `redemptions.csv` | a points redemption | `date`, `employee_id`, `points`, `reward_category`, `delivery_type`, `delivery_days` |
| `manager_weeks.csv` | a manager in an active week | `manager_id`, `week_start`, `sent` (0/1), `variant`, `period` (`pre` or `post`) |
| `experiment_assignments.csv` | a team in the test | `team_id`, `variant` (`nudge` or `control`), `assignment_date` |

## What is planted, and what is not

- Planted on purpose: a launch spike that fades, department differences, 40% of people who never send, a few popular people who receive most recognition, and a manager nudge that raises how often managers recognise (from 7 Sep 2026).
- Not claimed: that any of this matches a real company. The nudge effect was set by the script, so the dashboard demonstrates the analysis method, not a real result.

## How the test is analysed

1. Teams are randomised in pairs, matched on department and on each manager's baseline activity.
2. Outcome: share of manager-weeks with at least one recognition sent, per manager.
3. Primary estimate: post-period rate regressed on the nudge flag and the manager's pre-period rate (a baseline-adjusted estimate), with a 95% interval.
4. Also shown: the raw gap (not significant on its own), the smallest effect this sample could detect, a secondary metric (teammates recognised) and a guardrail (message length).

## Power BI measures (paste into a new measure each)

I could not run Power BI in my environment, so test these on your copy before using them. Load the six CSVs as tables named `Employees`, `Teams`, `Recognitions`, `Redemptions`, `ManagerWeeks`, `Experiments`, and relate `employee_id` and `team_id` where they match.

```DAX
Invited = COUNTROWS ( Employees )

Logged In =
CALCULATE ( COUNTROWS ( Employees ), NOT ( ISBLANK ( Employees[first_login_date] ) ) )

Login Rate = DIVIDE ( [Logged In], [Invited] )

Human Recognitions =
CALCULATE ( COUNTROWS ( Recognitions ), Recognitions[giver_id] <> "SYSTEM" )

Participation 30d =
VAR EndDate = MAX ( Recognitions[date] )
VAR Win =
    FILTER (
        ALL ( Recognitions ),
        Recognitions[date] > EndDate - 30
            && Recognitions[date] <= EndDate
            && Recognitions[giver_id] <> "SYSTEM"
    )
VAR Active =
    DISTINCT (
        UNION (
            SELECTCOLUMNS ( Win, "id", Recognitions[giver_id] ),
            SELECTCOLUMNS ( Win, "id", Recognitions[receiver_id] )
        )
    )
RETURN DIVIDE ( COUNTROWS ( Active ), [Invited] )

Manager Weekly Rate = AVERAGE ( ManagerWeeks[sent] )

Redemption Rate =
DIVIDE ( DISTINCTCOUNT ( Redemptions[employee_id] ), [Logged In] )

Avg Standard Delivery Days =
CALCULATE (
    AVERAGE ( Redemptions[delivery_days] ),
    Redemptions[delivery_type] = "Standard"
)
```
